_note: Interaction-role-local recipes that EXTEND the shared playbook (../../frontend-design/references/interaction_playbook.json — recipes, universal_engine, verify_coexistence, centerpiece_doctrine). Read the shared playbook in full first; the entries here are the additional, harvested patterns the Interaction Engineer owns that the shared playbook does not yet carry. Everything here is portable to ONE self-contained index.html, no build step, runs on file://.

interactive_hero_verify_coexist.job: A clickable HERO that is BOTH an interactive trigger (Verify OFF) AND a single Verify provenance hit-target (Verify ON) — e.g. a 'pick a side' hero where each half runs the model and reveals a result, but turning Verify on makes the whole hero one auditable claim. The reusable pattern for ANY interactive element that must COEXIST with the Verify/Inspector layer over a provenance-bearing container. THIS IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE REUSABLE INTERACTION RULE: get it right and every playground composes cleanly with the audit layer.
the_three_rules: 1. role=link sub-targets, OUTSIDE the Verify allow-list. The interactive sub-targets are `role="link" tabindex="0"` elements (NOT <button>/<a href>/<input>/<select> — i.e. NOT in the Verify engine's INNER_INTERACTIVE allow-list), laid over a CONTAINER that carries the provenance `data-*` (e.g. the .teaser carries data-des). Because the halves are not in INNER_INTERACTIVE, the Verify engine does not treat them as 'real inner controls to defer to', so a click on a half, when Verify is on, BUBBLES UP to the container's provenance hit.

2. Every feature handler early-returns under Verify. EVERY feature handler (the interactive behaviour) starts with `if (document.documentElement.classList.contains('verify-on')) return;` (the shared `vOn()` helper) — on click, on keydown(Enter/Space), AND on hover/focus side-effects. Under Verify the gesture does nothing in feature-land, so it falls through to the Verify layer.

3. Feature code NEVER calls stopPropagation. Feature handlers must NOT call `stopPropagation()` (nor a `preventDefault()` that swallows the bubble). The click must be free to bubble to the container so the Verify engine's delegated handler catches it and opens the provenance drawer.

RESULT: Verify OFF -> the halves are interactive (pick a side -> run the model -> reveal the picked team's championship probability). Verify ON -> the click bubbles to the container's provenance hit and opens the drawer. ONE element, two honest modes, no double-fire.
interactive_hero_verify_coexist.why_role_link: The Verify engine defers to genuine inner controls (its INNER_INTERACTIVE selector is roughly `a[href],button,select,input,textarea,label,summary,details,[role='tab'],[role='button']:not(.v-hit),.rt-card,.pred-tabs,.controls` so it does NOT hijack a real form control's own behaviour). A clickable hero half must therefore be OUTSIDE that allow-list so the engine lets its click bubble to the container under Verify. `role="link"` + `tabindex="0"` gives it link semantics + keyboard focus WITHOUT being an `<a href>` (which IS in the allow-list). Keyboard activation is wired manually (Enter/Space -> the feature, also guarded by vOn()).
interactive_hero_verify_coexist.a11y_and_degradation: Each half has an aria-label describing the ACTION (not just the team), is keyboard-focusable (tabindex=0) and Enter/Space-activates. The reveal degrades to the published number in prose if JS is off. Decorative hero overlays (ability chips, particle canvas, lightning bolt) use pointer-events:none and carry NO data-* so they never intercept either the halves or the Verify hit. Each half keeps the >=44px hit-area floor (shared playbook control_specs).
interactive_hero_verify_coexist.verify_keying: Provenance stays on the CONTAINER — ONE data-des for the whole hero. Do NOT put a data-* id on each half (that would make each half its own hit and split the hero into two claims). Register ONE verify_map entry for the container's id (kind:generated/media for a hero video/still). The interactive reveal recomputes via the client_model but is NOT itself a separate provenance claim.
interactive_hero_verify_coexist.generalizes_to: Any element that must be interactive AND a single Verify hit: a clickable map region over a provenance container, a tappable chart area, a 'choose your scenario' band. The recipe is always the same three rules: sub-targets are role=link (out of INNER_INTERACTIVE) + every feature handler early-returns under verify-on + feature code never stopPropagation -> the gesture is interactive off-Verify and bubbles to the container's provenance hit on-Verify.
anti_patterns: Making the halves <button>/<a href> (they land IN INNER_INTERACTIVE, so under Verify the engine defers to them and the click never reaches the container — the hero stops being auditable).
Calling stopPropagation() in a feature handler (kills the bubble; Verify can never catch the click).
Forgetting the vOn() guard on a hover/focus side-effect (the hero visibly reacts under Verify, confusing 'is this audit or play?').
Tagging each half with its own data-* (splits one hero claim into many hits).
interactive_hero_verify_coexist.when: Any interactive HERO (or interactive element over a provenance container) on a blog that ships the Verify/Inspector layer — which is every blog. See also the shared playbook `verify_coexistence` (the general control-handler guard) and the Programmer's component_implementations.json E1 interactive-hero (the build wiring).

share_result_card._alias: share / copy my result — the CRASH-PROOF pattern (never the Web Share API)
share_result_card.job: Let a reader SHARE the result of an interactive (their pick's championship probability, their quiz score, their tuned scenario) as a small result-CARD image + a one-line text — pasteable into chat/social as a picture AND into a text field as text — with an always-present Download link. The hard rule: do this with the CLIPBOARD + a canvas card, NEVER with the Web Share API.
share_result_card.the_rule: DO NOT call the Web Share API (`navigator.share(...)` / `navigator.canShare(...)`) with a File payload. Handing it a File makes the renderer send the browser an IPC the browser REJECTS, which CRASHES THE WHOLE TAB ('Aw, Snap!', RESULT_CODE_KILLED_BAD_MESSAGE) — a renderer-process crash BELOW the JS layer, so `try/catch` and promise `.catch()` cannot intercept it. A `file://` origin (how the blog is previewed locally) is the most reliable trigger. There is no try/catch that makes the Web Share API File path safe; replace it entirely with clipboard-copy + download (PIT-66).
the_three_rules: 1. Copy a CARD IMAGE + text to the clipboard, not a File to the OS share sheet. Use `navigator.clipboard.write([new ClipboardItem({'image/png': blob, 'text/plain': textBlob})])` — this pastes as a PICTURE into chat/social AND as TEXT into a text field. Fall back to `navigator.clipboard.writeText(text)` when ClipboardItem/image-copy is unsupported, and ALWAYS render a Download-card <a download> link as the universal floor (every platform, every origin).

2. Build the image Blob SYNCHRONOUSLY, inside the click's user-activation window. Draw the card on a 2D <canvas> and convert via `canvas.toDataURL('image/png')` -> Blob (a small dataURL->Blob helper) — NOT async `canvas.toBlob`. An async toBlob defers past the transient user-activation, and the clipboard write then REJECTS. So the share entry point must get the Blob back synchronously (pass a callback that the synchronous toDataURL path fires before it returns), then do the clipboard write in the same gesture tick.

3. Never leak a file:// URL in the share text. Gate any URL placed in the text payload to http(s) origins only (e.g. only include `location.href` when `location.protocol` starts with 'http') — a local preview's file:// path is useless and leaks the author's disk path. Keep the text honest (the page's real title + canonical URL), no overclaiming.
anti_patterns: Calling navigator.share({files:[file]}) / navigator.canShare({files}) anywhere — it crashes the whole tab on file:// (and some https Chrome builds) with a renderer-process crash try/catch cannot catch. There is NO safe try/catch wrapper for it.
Building the card Blob with async canvas.toBlob (or any await before the clipboard write) — the user-activation window is lost and navigator.clipboard.write then rejects, so nothing copies.
Putting location.href in the share text unconditionally — on a local file:// preview that leaks the author's disk path and is useless to the reader. Gate it to http(s).
Shipping ONLY a clipboard copy with no Download link — the clipboard write can be denied by permissions/unsupported; the <a download> card is the universal floor that always works.
share_result_card.when: Any 'share / copy my result' control on a blog — after an interactive reveals a number (a pick's probability, a quiz score, a tuned scenario). Reference implementation: the WC blog `wirePickerAndShare` / `doShare` / `buildCardBlob` / `clipboardFallback` (synchronous toDataURL->Blob, ClipboardItem image+text, writeText fallback, download-card, no Web Share API). cf PIT-66, PIT-08 (the user-activation gesture window the clipboard write must stay inside).
